Every stated requirement maps to a V6 signal or graph check (build.py asserts it). The run sentence is stated. Every observation point names its file and item type (float), and the type is in the sink params. There are 13 distinct mutants: header order and sign, header length, payload lengths, three wrong-tap rewires, both unperturbed streams, the mid-capture swap, and the Throttle bypass. Disjointness names the nearest training specs. The GPL attribution and the stripped options metadata (author David Pi, copyright, title, description) are recorded. rejected.reason: A header-after-frame mutant cannot be expressed as one edit-operator call on this reference, and gates.py applies exactly one operator per mutant. The Stream Mux always starts with input 0, which holds frame_header. Moving the header after the frame needs at least two changes: stream A rewired to input 0, the header moved to the last input, and the lengths reordered. The reviewer's 'more simple' single rewire, rewire_input(blocks_stream_mux_0, port 2, frame_header), was built and run (p_single_rewire_hdr_port2). It produces -1, -2, 1, 2, 3, 4, -1, -2, -1, ...: a payload error that still starts with the header, not header-after-frame. It is a wrong-source fault on a mux input, the same kind as existing mutants 5 and 6. set_param on lengths alone keeps the header first. bypass and delete_connection make the graph fail at V3. The property is therefore covered by the two verified probes listed under compliance:F3.
